item.title: Bitcoinpolitisk institutt Norge – Bitcoin er tid
item.description:
Hva har penger med tid og fysikk å gjøre? Og er bitcoin i bunn og grunn en desentralisert klokke?


«Pengar er storkna mannesveitte», skrev Aasmund Olavsson Vinje. Arbeidet blir gjort nå, men pengene lar oss ta med resultatet av arbeidet inn i fremtiden.


I over hundre år har økonomer, ingeniører og tenkere lett etter sammenhengen mellom penger og den fysiske verden. H.G. Wells og John Maynard Keynes diskuterte energistandarder. Henry Ford ville ha en valuta knyttet til energi. Frederick Soddy og Buckminster Fuller mente at penger må forstås i lys av arbeid, energi og termodynamikk.


Bitcoin oppfyller ikke alle disse drømmene. Men systemet ga et nytt svar på et gammelt problem: Hvordan lager man penger på internett uten en sentral bokholder? Svaret er proof-of-work. Energi og datakraft bygger en felles historikk som blir stadig vanskeligere å skrive om, og nettverket holder selv takten på omtrent én ny blokk hvert tiende minutt.


I denne Satoshi-samtalen holder Andreas Schjønhaug foredrag om penger, fysikk og tid, og om hvorfor bitcoin kanskje best kan forstås som en klokke uten urmaker. Filosofen Sæbjørn Forberg kommenterer.


Medvirkende:

Andreas Schjønhaug, innleder

Sæbjørn Forberg, filosof og kommentator

Emil Nygaard Nilsen, teknolog og nestleder i Bitcoinpolitisk institutt Norge, ordstyrer


Spilt inn på Litteraturhuset i Oslo 11. november 2026.


Bli medlem eller støtt arbeidet vårt: https://bpinorge.no

X: @BPInorge

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/bitcoinpolitisk-institutt-norge

The Bitcoin Street Journal Market Update – Trump Picks Peirce's SEC Successor, Bitcoin Loses $70K in Extreme Fear | Morning Edition
item.description:
Friday the 13th Morning Edition: the White House names four new picks for the SEC and CFTC, including Steven Levine for Hester Peirce's old seat. Bitcoin slips below $70,000, Fear and Greed drops to Extreme Fear, and two treasury companies show how fast borrowed money turns into pressure.

THE MARKET TODAY

- Bitcoin: $69,058, down 6.1% in 24 hours (range $67,922 to $73,602); down 8.7% on the week, 17.2% on the month

- Ether: $1,942, down about 5%

- Total crypto market: about $2.34 trillion, down 7.1%; Bitcoin dominance 59.0%

- Fear and Greed: 20, Extreme Fear (from 28)

- Bitcoin is about 45% below its $126,080 all-time high

NEW REFEREES

- Cointelegraph: Trump nominates Steven Levine to replace Hester Peirce at the SEC, and former CFTC commissioner Kristin Johnson for the seat held by Caroline Crenshaw

- The SEC has two of five seats filled; CFTC Chairman Michael Selig sits alone

- Democrats take the Senate in January, so the confirmation window is narrow

UNDER SEVENTY

- The Block: $798M liquidated in four hours, $718.5M of it longs

- CoinDesk: dollar index at a 19-month high; spot Bitcoin ETFs now down over $1.5B in net outflows for the year

DEBT COMES DUE

- CoinDesk: Nakamoto owes Kraken $165M, more than its market value, with about 70% of its coins pledged

- CoinDesk: BTCS sold ether at a loss to protect a $64M Aave loan

- CoinDesk: SpaceX-Tesla merger talks put about 30,000 BTC in focus

BUILDING THROUGH THE STORM

- U.Today: Ripple's RLUSD passes PayPal's PYUSD at $2.71B

- The Block: TRM Labs launches a service to help police seize stolen crypto in minutes

- DOJ moves to seize $1.2B stolen from Binance and takes down the FaceStealer deepfake scam

- U.Today: two Satoshi-era addresses holding 100 BTC wake up after 16 years

SPEED ROUND

- XRP Ledger upgrade on December 3 with a fix for slow ledger closures

- Gemini trading volume down 73%, Q3 revenue $41M

- Louisiana sues Kalshi, Robinhood and other prediction markets

- Maple Finance co-founder and COO depart

NOSTR DESK

- Lessons from 16-year-old coins: your Nostr key is your identity, so back it up offline and plan who can find it

ON THE SITE TODAY

- News Explorer: follow the SEC and CFTC confirmation hearings

- Top Gainers and Losers: see which coins held up in the sell-off

- Digital Asset Treasury Tracker: who's holding, who's borrowing, who's selling

- Bitcoin Guides: the early days of Bitcoin, explained

ADVERTISE

Reach readers who check the news before the market opens. Site-wide display, daily newsletter sponsorships, sponsor reads on this podcast and posts to our Nostr followers, bundled into custom packages. thebitcoinstreetjournal.com/advertise

LISTEN ANYWHERE

Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Pandora, iHeartRadio, Fountain, Pocket Casts, Podcast Addict, and The Bitcoin Street Journal on YouTube. All links: thebitcoinstreetjournal.com/podcast/

Follow, rate and share.

General information only, not investment advice.

item.title: Bitcoin Takeover Podcast – S17 E51: Martti Malmi on Iris, NostrVPN and Freedom Tech
item.description:
We recorded this at Bitcoin Amsterdam, the Bitcoin Magazine conference, with legendary cypherpunk and Satoshi contributor Martti Malmi. This is his second time on the show. Two years ago in Prague we talked about 2009, the forum, and the man who signed his emails Satoshi Nakamoto. This time I had promised we would talk about what he is building now. The conference still put him on a history panel.

Martti would rather talk about Iris, the Nostr client at iris.to, and especially NostrVPN, which he describes as Tailscale without the Tailscale company: your devices find each other on Nostr, with no email login and no coordination server. Underneath is FIPS, an ad-hoc mesh routing protocol. He also walks through Iris Chat, Iris Drive, git.iris.to, Hashtree, and a directory of about 20 apps at apps.iris.to. He is not making money from any of it, and he does not think software is a great business model anymore. Finnish people, he says, tend to be a bit ideological and not great businessmen. Maybe he is the same way.

We talk about Nostr in a bear market, about building for AI agents versus building for humans, and about permissionlessness as the reason an agent might pick Nostr at all. I put my usual heresy to him, that Bitcoin is now a family of projects, and he stays open-minded: if network effects dissolve, funds may gravitate to the best store of value and the best way to pay, and the biggest network may matter less. For him, Bitcoin is still mostly a store of value. He would like to tap to pay and not have to tell the merchant he wants to pay in Bitcoin.

We do break the "no Satoshi" rule twice. Martti is the one who set bitcoin.org up on WordPress, and he still thinks the man who struggled with that setup was "just a guy," unless you prefer the joke that the integer overflow bug was planted to make a time-travelling AI look human. And he remembers Satoshi paying him for the website work in US dollars, in an envelope, sent to his father's address so it would not sit on a dorm floor. He does not have the original envelope. His grandfather, in 2009, thought this could become a global reserve currency, and did not buy any. Years later, after another crash headline, his father messaged him: "I hope you sold early." And he did.

In between there is the year he stopped writing code himself, "meat agents" in smart glasses, a romantic argument that the best life extension technology is having kids, Michael Pollan on simulated feeling, and a fifty-percent kind of optimism about permissionless tech. You can find him on Nostr as Sirius, at iris.to/sirius. The name comes from the pun, the star, and Sirius Black.

What we cover:

  • Why history panels still haunt him, and why he wanted to shill the new work
  • NostrVPN as a peer-to-peer Tailscale alternative, and FIPS mesh routing
  • Iris Chat, Iris Drive, git.iris.to, Hashtree, and the apps.iris.to directory
  • Why he is not trying to make money from software
  • Nostr's chicken-and-egg problem, bots, and a bet on agentic use
  • Whether we are building for humans or for agents
  • Bitcoin as a family of projects, and dissolving network effects
  • Payments, Lightning, Square, BTCPay, and tap to pay
  • The bitcoin.org WordPress story, and "oh, he's just a guy"
  • The year he wrote no code, longevity, and consciousness
  • Satoshi, an envelope of dollars, and "I hope you sold early"
  • How to find him: Sirius, iris.to/sirius, and the three links to try first

This episode is sponsored by SideShift, Cake Wallet, eCash / LayerTwo Labs, Braiins Hashpower, and Orange Rock.

The previous conversation is S16 E12: Martti Malmi on Bitcoin in 2009 & Satoshi Nakamoto, at bitcoin-takeover.com/s16-e12-martti-malmi-on-bitcoin-in-2009-satoshi-nakamoto/. His published correspondence with Satoshi is at mmalmi.github.io/satoshi/. The full Bitcoin Takeover archive is at bitcoin-takeover.com.

item.title: Bitcoin Today Recast – Bitcoin Breaks Under $72K as MSCI Drops Strategy
item.description:
Humble Warrior hosts Bitcoin Today while Loren drives home, and the room works through a brutal morning: the price sliding under seventy-two thousand, Strategy getting dropped from the MSCI indexes, ETF flows getting worse, and Jensen Huang out at Nvidia. The debate runs the full arc, from whether $71,000 is just honest demand and pain is what brings people to Bitcoin, to the case that adoption comes from America, from community, and from outside the ETF wrapper. Richard Greaser argues the American case, the room fights over self-custody versus exchanges, and it closes with a simple rule for a normal bear market: control your stack and live your life.


Loren Hodl and Terence Michael host Bitcoin Today live on X, weekdays at 8:30 AM PT. (Note: Humble Warrior guest hosted today's episode.)


YouTube: https://youtube.com/@lorenhodl

X: @LorenHodl @HumbleWarrior @GreaserRichard


Chapters:

item.title: What Bitcoin Did – Can Bitcoin Survive If AI Breaks Encryption? | Michael Dunworth
item.description:
“We’re playing for the machines. We just don’t know it yet.”

Michael Dunworth joins the show to explain why he’s willing to bet a Bitcoin that RSA encryption will be broken within ten years, and why he believes Bitcoiners need to rethink their security assumptions.

We discuss AI-assisted hacking, the risks of third-party services, and why a customer data leak can turn into a physical security threat. Michael explains why he thinks Bitcoin’s social layer is weakening, while we debate development priorities and the trade-offs involved in changing the protocol.

We also discuss AI’s appetite for data and energy, what happens to privacy if encrypted information becomes accessible, and Michael’s theories about reconstructing past events. Finally, we explore what money and community could look like in that future, and whether Bitcoin could become a ledger of truth for machines.

item.title: The Bitcoin Treasuries Podcast with Tim Kotzman – How Early Bitcoiners Protect Generational Wealth Beyond Self-Custody | Matt McClintock
item.description:
Matt McClintock, CEO and Co-founder of Bespoke Group, joins the show to discuss how a 2017 introduction to a family with about $150 million in Bitcoin pulled an estate planning attorney into a new kind of family office, and why he closed his law practice in 2024 to build it. He talks about early clients who held about 90% of their wealth in Bitcoin, why most of them are net sellers today, and the four places he says wealth can go: consumption, inheritance, taxes, and philanthropy. He also explains why those clients aren't interested in Bitcoin treasury companies or digital credit — they already have the asset — and walks through the Sovereignty Paradox: why "not your keys, not your coins" breaks down under the weight of generational wealth, and how qualified custody and legal structures help shift that risk.


Disclaimer: NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE - For entertainment purposes only.


Today's episode is brought to you by www.cakewallet.com/install and www.quantifyfunds.com.


Tim Kotzman on X: https://x.com/TimKotzman

Matt McClintock on X: https://x.com/mcclintock_m

5:06 - Early clients with 90% of their wealth in Bitcoin

8:22 - What a family office actually is

item.description:
Bram Kanstein is a creative entrepreneur and the host of Bitcoin for Millennials, exploring Bitcoin not as a trade, but as essential savings technology and a rational opt-out from a failing fiat money system.

🔔 SUBSCRIBE TO GET NOTIFIED

› https://youtube.com/@bramk⁠⁠

› https://x.com/bramk


🕑 TIMESTAMPS

00:00 - Intro: everything digital can be copied

01:30 - Money is a ruler

04:21 - Why the machine economy needs a fixed ruler

05:20 - Property 1: it gives the digital world a clock

07:12 - Property 2: its creation is tethered to energy

10:49 - Property 3: the first digital thing that can be yours

12:07 - Property 4: it moves anywhere, for anyone or anything

13:37 - Property 5: it can't be banned, it's an idea

14:45 - Property 6: the map is the territory, anyone can audit it

18:05 - Property 7: no center, no closing hours, no bouncer

19:42 - Property 8: it is nobody's promise

21:56 - The agentic economy needs its gold layer

22:32 - What has value when everything can be copied


ℹ️ EPISODE SUMMARY

Bram Kanstein discusses what still has value when AI can copy everything digital. He starts with the kilogram, a metal cylinder in a vault near Paris that drifted until it was tied to a constant in 2019. Money never got that moment: the dollar has lost more than 95 percent of its purchasing power since 1913. He walks through eight properties that tie Bitcoin to the two things AI can't copy, energy and time. Dollars can be the medium, but the machine economy needs a ruler that doesn't move.

item.title: The Wolf Of All Streets – Wall Street's Bitcoin Bet Has A Hidden Problem l Mark Yusko
item.description:
Mark Yusko, founder and CIO of Morgan Creek Capital Management, joins Scott Melker on The Wolf Of All Streets to unpack MSCI dropping Strategy and MetaPlanet from its indexes, the NVIDIA CEO scandal, and where Bitcoin sits in the cycle.

Scott and Mark open with Jensen Huang's resignation and what it means for NVIDIA and the AI trade, then dig into the MSCI index decision and why it matters for MSTR and Bitcoin. They also cover the Anthropic IPO debate, AI tools and costs, Mark's cycle view from winter to spring, leverage in the stock market, and how pod-shop hedge funds get forced to cut risk.

In this episode:
00:00 MSCI delistings and the Jensen Huang scandal
03:01 Jensen Huang resigns from NVIDIA
16:02 NVIDIA, interest rates and the AI trade
21:01 MSCI drops Strategy and MetaPlanet
24:02 Anthropic IPO and AI hype

item.title: Onramp Bitcoin Media – Bitcoin Did This Before. Then It Went 6X.
item.description:
Through Dec 31: $100/month (or $1,000/year) for your first year of Multi-Institution Custody, normally $2,400. Open a vault, set up a recurring buy, and use code TLT at onrampbitcoin.com. Discounted pricing covers vaults holding up to 25 BTC.


Bitcoin is back where it was five years ago, and it sits beside gold as one of 2026's two worst major assets, a first in Charlie Bilello's data. Jackson, Michael and Brian explain why that makes inflation protection cheap before the big print.


BOOK A CONSULTATION

Holding Bitcoin for decades raises two questions: who protects it, and how it reaches your family. Onramp answers both. Three institutions protect it, and no single one can lose it, move it, or use it. Inheritance built in. Insured through Lloyd's of London. Speak with our team to see if it fits.

👉 https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/consult-tlt-pod


GET ON THE LIST

Our research, event invites, and the week's Bitcoin news in one free email.

📩 https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/research-tlt-pod


ABOUT THIS EPISODE

Brian opens on the complaint everywhere this week, no gains in five years, and answers it with 2017: the top, the flat years, and what came next. Jackson and Michael cover the launch of Onramp's custody for businesses and why dollar-cost averaging holds up through a drawdown. Then the Jensen Huang scandal, why Nvidia is practically the market, and Anthropic's IPO as the AI trade's next test. Ledger CEO Pascal Gauthier's warning that everyone gets hacked eventually leads to the bigger question: how Bitcoin scales to a million dollars without one failure knocking holders out of the game. Macroscope's big print thesis says inflation protection gets sold cheap before the printing starts, and Brian points to COVID as the last time it happened. The quick hits close on Bilello's stat that Bitcoin and gold are down together, plus Coinbase's federal trust charter and BlackRock's record in-kind conversions.

item.title: Rob Wallace | Bitcoin News – The AI Crash Last Week Was Sniffing Out Something BIG | Mark Suman and Liam Nelson
item.description:
🔴 LIVE | Super AI is driving the cost of intelligence toward the cost of the electricity behind it, which means expert-level medicine, law, engineering and education for roughly the price of light.

@marksuman of Maple AI and @Lnelson_21 break down Early Riders’ Singularity Stack thesis and why Bitcoin, not AI stocks, is the ultimate winner of the AI trade.

Savers on gold-backed money once saw railroads and cheap steel arrive as rising purchasing power, and the same transition is now running at the singularity’s pace. In dollar terms those gains get inflated away, while Bitcoin’s fixed supply captures them directly.

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Interviews – Yoni Assia: AI Trading, Bitcoin's $250K Target and Tokenized Markets
item.description:
Could talking to an AI agent become the normal way to manage an investment portfolio?


eToro CEO and co-founder Yoni Assia joins Graham Stone on Bitcoin.com's Live News Desk at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026 to discuss the next phase of trading, where AI assistants can analyze markets, access portfolio information, and execute trades on behalf of investors


Assia expects agents to account for most of eToro's trading volume by the end of 2027, although he acknowledges that trust and safeguards remain major obstacles.


The conversation also explores his $250,000 Bitcoin prediction for 2030, the evolution of 24/7 tokenized financial markets, and eToro's expansion into self-custody through its acquisition of Zengo.

item.title: Once Bitten! A Bitcoin Podcast. – Faketoshi Part 3 - The Saga Ends Here - Mark Hunter & Arthur Van Pelt - #625
item.description:
Faketoshi: Fraud, Lies and the Battle for Bitcoin’s Soul.

$ BTC 74,026

Block height 975,450

For this episode I am rejoined with researchers Mark Hunter and Arthur Van Pelt, who discuss part 3 of their trilogy series 'Faketoshi' and detail the extensive legal frauds perpetrated by Australian IT consultant (D.r) Craig Wright.

Key Topics:

  • The COPA v. Craig Wright trial
  • Evidence of systematic document forgery
  • Craig Wright's false claims to be Satoshi Nakamoto
  • The role of Calvin Ayre in funding Wright's litigation
  • Psychological analysis of cult-like followings Find the series here: https://faketoshi.co.uk/ Arthur van Pelt - @ArthurvanPelt

Arthur is a Bitcoin consultant who began mapping out the depth and breadth of Wright’s illegal operations in 2019, becoming renowned as the world’s foremost Craig Wright critic.

Mark Hunter - @Twentynothing00

Mark is an author and ghostwriter who has worked in the blockchain/crypto sector since 2017. He is also the author of Ultimate Catastrophe – How MtGox Lost Half a Billion Dollars and Nearly Killed Bitcoin, the first book to tell the full story of the rise and fall of Bitcoin exchange MtGox.

item.title: Sound Money Bitcoin Podcast – #351 Das Wunder von Wörgl - Gemeinde druckt eigenes Geld, Nationalbank zieht den Stecker
item.description:
Im Sommer 1932, mitten in der Weltwirtschaftskrise, wagt das kleine Tiroler Wörgl ein Experiment, das weltweit für Aufsehen sorgt: Bürgermeister Michael Unterguggenberger lässt eigenes Geld drucken. Das Besondere daran ist, dass die sogenannten Arbeitswertscheine jeden Monat 1 % an Wert verlieren. Wer sie hortet, verliert also Geld, und genau das bringt die Wirtschaft im Ort wieder in Schwung. Doch dann schreitet die Österreichische Nationalbank ein und beendet das Experiment.

Ich habe mich dafür auf den Weg nach Wörgl gemacht und mit Veronika Spielbichler gesprochen, der Vorsitzenden des Unterguggenberger Instituts. Wir sprechen darüber, wie das Freigeld technisch funktionierte, welche Rolle die Ideen von Silvio Gesell spielten, was mit dem Geld gebaut wurde und warum das Experiment verboten wurde.

Außerdem schlagen wir die Brücke ins Heute: Ist unsere Inflation nicht auch eine Form von Schwundgeld, nur ohne Stempelmarke?

War das Wunder von Wörgl also ein echtes Wirtschaftswunder, oder ist der Mythos über die Jahrzehnte einfach immer größer geworden?

item.itunes:summary:
Im Sommer 1932, mitten in der Weltwirtschaftskrise, wagt das kleine Tiroler Wörgl ein Experiment, das weltweit für Aufsehen sorgt: Bürgermeister Michael Unterguggenberger lässt eigenes Geld drucken. Das Besondere daran ist, dass die sogenannten Arbeitswertscheine jeden Monat 1 % an Wert verlieren. Wer sie hortet, verliert also Geld, und genau das bringt die Wirtschaft im Ort wieder in Schwung. Doch dann schreitet die Österreichische Nationalbank ein und beendet das Experiment.

Ich habe mich dafür auf den Weg nach Wörgl gemacht und mit Veronika Spielbichler gesprochen, der Vorsitzenden des Unterguggenberger Instituts. Wir sprechen darüber, wie das Freigeld technisch funktionierte, welche Rolle die Ideen von Silvio Gesell spielten, was mit dem Geld gebaut wurde und warum das Experiment verboten wurde.

Außerdem schlagen wir die Brücke ins Heute: Ist unsere Inflation nicht auch eine Form von Schwundgeld, nur ohne Stempelmarke?

War das Wunder von Wörgl also ein echtes Wirtschaftswunder, oder ist der Mythos über die Jahrzehnte einfach immer größer geworden?

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Weekly Update – Bank Collapse Topples a President + Warren’s Crypto Comeback | The Weekly
item.description:
A major bank collapse in Paraguay has triggered a political crisis, leaving millions of customers caught in the fallout and the country’s president removed from office.


In this episode of The Weekly, Alex Richardson and Jamie Redman unpack what the crisis reveals about the risks inside traditional finance and whether crypto’s transparency offers a meaningful alternative.

They also break down the growing backlash against tokenized stocks, with roughly 90% of the companies originally targeted by the OKX-ICE platform reportedly objecting to the initiative.


Plus, the episode covers Elizabeth Warren’s potential return to a more powerful role overseeing banking and crypto policy, Vitalik Buterin’s evolving case for ETH as money and a store of value, and World Liberty Financial’s latest WLFI token buyback amid renewed political scrutiny.


In this episode:

  • How a bank collapse escalated into a political crisis in Paraguay
  • What the fallout says about transparency in traditional finance
  • Why companies are pushing back against tokenized stocks
  • What greater influence for Elizabeth Warren could mean for crypto
  • Vitalik Buterin’s argument for ETH as money and a store of value
  • Why World Liberty Financial is buying back WLFI again

item.title: Einfach Bitcoin Podcast – Seed Phrase sicher aufbewahren: Die wichtigsten Fehler vermeiden
item.description:
---werbung---
Bitcoin GRATIS eBook
https://klick.short.gy/Bitcoin-eBook
---werbung---


❤️ Danke für deine Unterstützung!

Jede Folge kostet Zeit und Herzblut. Wenn dir der Podcast gefällt, freue ich mich über ein kleines Trinkgeld. Schon der Preis eines Kaffees macht einen Unterschied.

☕ Kaffee ausgeben: klick hier

 
Eine Seed Phrase wirkt unscheinbar: eine Folge gewöhnlicher Wörter, die man aufschreibt und anschließend gut weglegt. Bei einer selbstverwalteten Bitcoin-Wallet ist sie jedoch der zentrale Wiederherstellungsschlüssel. Wer diese Wörter besitzt, kann je nach Wallet-Standard den Zugang zu den damit verbundenen Bitcoin wiederherstellen. Wer sie verliert, kann sich selbst aussperren. Wer sie weitergibt, kann die Kontrolle abgeben. Deshalb geht es bei der Seed Phrase nicht um Geheimniskrämerei, sondern um eine klare Sicherheitsentscheidung. 

Die Seed Phrase ist kein Passwort, das zurückgesetzt werden kann 

Sie rekonstruiert den Zugang zur Wallet 

Moderne Wallets leiten viele Schlüssel aus einem gemeinsamen Ausgangspunkt ab. Die Seed Phrase bildet diesen Ausgangspunkt in lesbarer Form ab. Der BIP39-Standard beschreibt, wie eine Wortfolge in den Seed einer deterministischen Wallet umgewandelt werden kann. Das bedeutet praktisch: Die Wörter können wichtiger sein als das Gerät, auf dem die Wallet gerade installiert ist. Die technische Spezifikation von BIP39 erläutert den Mechanismus. 

Ein vergessener App-Code kann bei manchen Anwendungen unangenehm sein. Eine verlorene Seed Phrase ist grundsätzlich etwas anderes. Bei echter Selbstverwahrung gibt es keine zentrale Stelle, die sie kennt oder einen Ersatz ausstellen kann. Genau das schafft Unabhängigkeit von einem Anbieter, verlangt aber auch ein sorgfältiges Vorgehen. 

Digitale Kopien können aus Bequemlichkeit zum Risiko werden 

Ein Foto oder Cloud-Backup ist kein neutraler Aufbewahrungsort 

Ein Foto auf dem Smartphone, eine Notiz-App oder ein Dokument im E-Mail-Postfach fühlen sich praktisch an, weil sie überall verfügbar sind. Gleichzeitig können diese Daten durch kompromittierte Geräte, Synchronisierung, Backups oder unbefugte Zugriffe sichtbar werden. Auch der eigene Bildschirm ist nicht automatisch privat: Schadsoftware, Fernzugriff oder ein unaufmerksamer Moment können ausreichen, um ein Geheimnis zu kopieren. 

Das heißt nicht, dass Papier magisch sicher wäre. Es kann verbrennen, verloren gehen oder von anderen gefunden werden. Der entscheidende Punkt ist, die Angriffsflächen bewusst zu reduzieren. Eine Seed Phrase gehört nie in eine Chat-Nachricht, ein Formular, eine E-Mail oder auf eine Website. Seriöse Wallet-Anbieter fragen sie nicht ab, um angeblich ein Konto zu prüfen oder ein Problem zu lösen. 

Die häufigsten Fehler beginnen meist unter Zeitdruck 

Dringlichkeit ist ein typisches Warnsignal 

Viele Betrugsversuche arbeiten mit einem scheinbar akuten Problem: Eine Wallet müsse verifiziert werden, ein Guthaben sei gefährdet oder ein Update verlange sofortige Eingabe der Wörter. Die technische Realität ist einfacher: Wer die Seed Phrase kennt, kann den Zugang kontrollieren. Deshalb ist jede Aufforderung, sie preiszugeben, ein Grund, innezuhalten und den Vorgang abzubrechen. 

Auch ein schnell eingerichtetes Backup ohne Prüfung kann später problematisch werden. Ein Schreibfehler, die falsche Reihenfolge oder eine unleserliche Notiz sind keine kleinen Schönheitsfehler. Sie können eine Wiederherstellung verhindern. Sicherheit entsteht hier nicht durch Hektik, sondern durch einen nachvollziehbaren Prozess, den du selbst verstehst und bei dem niemand über deine Schulter schaut. 

Ein Backup muss gleichzeitig erreichbar und geschützt sein 

Denke in Risiken statt in einem einzigen perfekten Versteck 

Bei der Aufbewahrung geht es um mehrere Gefahren zugleich: Verlust durch Feuer oder Wasser, Diebstahl, neugierige Mitmenschen und den eigenen Vergessensfehler. Ein einziger ungeprüfter Zettel an einem offensichtlichen Ort löst dieses Problem nicht automatisch. Ebenso wenig ist es eine gute Idee, die Wörter auf viele Menschen zu verteilen, die nicht genau wissen, welche Verantwortung damit verbunden ist. 

Eine sinnvolle Lösung richtet sich nach dem Betrag, dem Wohnumfeld und dem eigenen Verständnis. Wichtig ist vor allem, dass du die Wiederherstellung nicht erst im Ernstfall gedanklich ausprobierst. Die österreichische Finanzmarktaufsicht beschreibt die sichere Verwahrung von Zugangsschlüsseln als zentrales Risiko bei Kryptowerten und weist darauf hin, dass Bedienfehler oder mangelhafte Datensicherung zu Verlusten führen können. Die FMA-Information ordnet diese Risiken ein. 

Sicherheit bedeutet auch, die eigenen Grenzen zu kennen 

Verwahrung durch einen Anbieter kann für manche Nutzer besser passen 

Selbstverwahrung wird im Bitcoin-Bereich oft als Ideal beschrieben. Sie ist aber kein Pflichtprogramm und keine Frage von Mut. Wer sich mit Backups, Wiederherstellung und technischen Sicherheitsfragen unwohl fühlt, sollte diese Unsicherheit ernst nehmen. Ein regulierter Verwahrdienst kann Risiken anders verteilen, bringt dafür Abhängigkeit vom Anbieter und dessen Regeln mit sich. 

Die passende Entscheidung ist keine Kaufempfehlung und lässt sich nicht pauschal treffen. Sie beginnt damit, die Unterschiede zu verstehen: Bei Selbstverwahrung liegt die Verantwortung für die Seed Phrase bei dir. Bei einer verwahrten Lösung liegt die Schlüsselverwaltung überwiegend beim Dienstleister. In beiden Fällen bleibt es wichtig, Betrugsversuche zu erkennen und Zugangsdaten sorgfältig zu schützen. 

Zusammenfassung 

Eine Seed Phrase ist der Wiederherstellungsschlüssel einer selbstverwalteten Bitcoin-Wallet. Sie darf weder fotografiert noch in Cloud-Diensten, Chats oder Formularen eingegeben werden. Besonders gefährlich sind Situationen mit künstlichem Zeitdruck und angeblichen Support-Anfragen. Gute Sicherheit heißt nicht, einem spektakulären Geheimversteck zu vertrauen. Sie heißt, den eigenen Zugang bewusst zu schützen, die Wiederherstellung zu verstehen und nur eine Verwahrungsform zu wählen, deren Verantwortung man wirklich tragen kann. 

Häufige Fragen zur Seed Phrase 

Darf ich meine Seed Phrase fotografieren? 

Nein. Ein Foto kann über Gerätespeicher, Cloud-Synchronisierung, Backups oder unbefugten Zugriff kopiert werden. Die Phrase sollte nicht als digitale Notiz oder Bilddatei abgelegt werden. 

Fragt ein seriöser Wallet-Support nach der Seed Phrase? 

Nein. Die Phrase ermöglicht die vollständige Wiederherstellung der Wallet. Eine Aufforderung zur Eingabe oder Übermittlung ist ein ernstes Warnsignal für Betrug. 

Kann ich eine verlorene Seed Phrase beim Anbieter zurücksetzen? 

Bei Selbstverwahrung grundsätzlich nicht. Die Wiederherstellungsinformationen liegen nur bei dir. Das ist ein zentraler Unterschied zu normalen Online-Konten. 

Reicht ein Passwort für den Schutz meiner Bitcoin? 

Ein Passwort kann ein Gerät oder eine Anwendung schützen, ersetzt aber nicht unbedingt die Seed Phrase. Wer die Wiederherstellungswörter besitzt, kann je nach Wallet den Zugang auf einem anderen Gerät wiederherstellen.

item.title: The Bitcoin Hole – The Future of Bitcoin Self-Custody
item.description:
We explore the latest in Bitcoin self-custody, from zero-click mobile exploits and cloud sync risks to hardware wallet server manipulation. We analyze FROST multisig for distributed trust and examine how open standards like BIP 138 and post-quantum research are future-proofing your digital gold.
Explore more at TheBitcoinHole.com, compare wallets, nodes, and self-custody hardware to take full control of your Bitcoin. https://thebitcoinhole.com
X / Twitter https://x.com/thebitcoinhole
YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@thebitcoinhole
Support the show https://ko-fi.com/thebitcoinhole

item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Was Familien heute wirklich belastet – Susanne Dröber über „Money Load“ im Familienalltag
item.description: 📖 „Money Load“ von Susanne Dröber erscheint am 7. Dezember – jetzt vorbestellen: https://aprycot.media/money-load/Zu wenig Zeit, zu wenig Geld, zu wenig Energie. Fast jede Familie, die ich kenne, spürt diesen Druck. Als Familienvater kenne ich ihn selbst. Susanne Dröber, Mutter von drei Kindern, Autorin und Podcasterin („Fix the Family“), hat sich gefragt, woher er eigentlich kommt. Ihre Antwort führt nicht zu Zeitmanagement-Tipps, sondern zu unserem Geld.Was wäre, wenn der Stress in vielen Familien gar kein persönliches Versagen ist, sondern im System steckt?👉 Wie ein Gespräch über Bitcoin und ein Nachmittag im Park zur Idee für „Money Load“ wurden👉 Warum Frauen heute arbeiten gehen dürfen, aber oft keine echte Wahl mehr haben👉 Wie sich das Hamsterrad selbst beschleunigt: Wer Zeit zurückkaufen will, braucht noch mehr Geld👉 Warum alle darüber reden, wie sie Geld verdienen, ausgeben und anlegen, aber kaum jemand das Geld selbst hinterfragt👉 Was Bitcoin Familien geben kann: Ruhe, Zuversicht und die Möglichkeit, bewusst auszusteigenMich hat in diesem Gespräch vor allem eine Frage nicht mehr losgelassen: Wie wollen wir Familie eigentlich wirklich leben? Nicht, wie wir alles irgendwie unterbekommen, sondern was uns wichtig ist. Susanne zeigt, dass diese Frage beim Geld anfängt, und dass wir heute zum ersten Mal eine echte Alternative haben.„Bitcoin ist Hoffnung, Zuversicht und die beste Chance, die wir aktuell haben.“ – Susanne Dröber📖 Das Buch„Money Load – Der unsichtbare Stress im Familienleben“Erscheint am 07.12.2026 bei Aprycot Media · Taschenbuch, 256 Seiten · ohne Vorwissen lesbarVorbestellen: https://aprycot.media/money-load/🔗 LinksSusannes Projekt „Fix the Family“: https://www.fixthefamily.net/Das Gespräch bei Niko Jilch („Was Bitcoin bringt“): https://youtu.be/lxh9HIoJ9OQ✨ Mein Ziel: Bitcoin verständlich machen – mit Geschichten, die zeigen, dass die ersten Schritte nicht groß sein müssen.👍 Gefällt dir die Folge? Abonnieren, liken und an jemanden schicken, der das hören sollte. item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – Inside BNY: Why the World's Largest Custodian Is Betting on Digital Money
item.description:
BNY's Nader Souri on stablecoins, OpenUSD, tokenized deposits and the infrastructure connecting traditional and digital finance

Accepting a stablecoin gives a company another way to get paid. Once the token reaches the wallet, the treasury team needs a way to put the proceeds to work. It can keep the token for another payment, redeem it for dollars or invest the proceeds under its cash policy. Each choice depends on what the company can hold and how quickly it can move the money again.

Nader Souri, head of digital and corporate banking at BNY, joins Jonas Gross and etonec’s Jonathan Knoll for the Digital Money Interview Series. Souri and Knoll worked together on Libra, when BNY explored how it might service the proposed reserve. They recall bringing legal and compliance teams into the work early. Souri explains how familiar tasks such as holding reserves and managing cash gave the bank a way to assess the proposal, and why he wanted regulators involved while the design was taking shape.

BNY’s work with Circle shows how those roles fit together today. Circle issues USDC. BNY is the primary reserve custodian and gives institutional clients a way to ask Circle to issue or redeem USDC through the bank’s platform. Souri explains why BNY wants to serve multiple issuers and why the same company might use a stablecoin to accept a payment and a tokenized deposit or money market fund to hold the proceeds.

The conversation covers the launch of Open USD and Qivalis’s plans for a euro stablecoin, as well as BNY’s expansion of digital asset custody to select EU institutions under MiCA. Souri expects collateral and liquidity movements to reach institutional scale early, with cross-border payments close behind. For corporate treasurers, he sees a more immediate hurdle. A wallet has to connect to the systems that already track cash and record transactions. That connection matters when a payment arrives outside banking hours and the company needs to move the proceeds to the account it uses to pay suppliers.

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – Can El Salvador Real Estate Prices Keep Skyrocketing? Watch THIS Before Buying in Bitcoin Country | Lexi Cross of GoodLife El Salvador
item.description:
Is El Salvador real estate overpriced, or is everyone who called El Zonte a bubble two years ago now wishing they’d bought? Lexi Cross thought prices were already too high back then, and they’ve gone up again since!

You’ve seen the headlines about El Salvador tourism and the apartment projects going up along the coast. What you can’t tell from outside is who’s buying now, what it takes to run a rental there, and which months are worth the trip.

Mike sits down with Lexi, who runs Good Life El Salvador with Chimbera and is on the show for the third time. Since her last visit they’ve started a rental management company, a hardwood furniture shop, and a free concierge service for people who want to see the country before they buy anything.

The buyer mix has changed. Lexi is taking more calls from Salvadorans coming home from the US, and they ask about San Miguel and Sonsonate while foreign buyers only ever ask about the coast. Then an email arrived from a client who went to her high school in Washington State.

Managing those units turned out harder than selling them. The railings rust and get cleaned every week. Guests want to bring pets. People negotiate the nightly rate, which Lexi never knew you could do. The cleaning fee on a two bedroom came in close to a hundred dollars, far higher than she’d planned. She’s also decided which properties she won’t manage, and she’s honest about why.

Then there’s timing. The best time to visit El Salvador depends on what you came for, and rainy season is the one most people skip for the wrong reasons. Mike and Lexi walk through when the rains arrive, what the waves do, and why bookings no longer collapse in the wet months. Mike’s place in punta mango had no rooms open on a weeknight in the middle of it.

For all the modernizing, Lexi says living in El Salvador is still an adventure, and that’s what makes this country special.

Whether you’re weighing moving to El Salvador or just trying to pick a week to come see it, listen before you book the flight.


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.title: On the Record by Bitcoin Policy UK – Response the FCA: how should the cryptoasset regulatory perimeter apply to Bitcoin?
item.description:
How should the UK’s new cryptoasset regulatory perimeter apply to Bitcoin?

In this AI-spoken episode, we present Bitcoin Policy UK’s response to the FCA’s consultation on its proposed Cryptoasset Perimeter Guidance.

BPUK welcomes the FCA’s recognition that developing software or participating in a decentralised network does not automatically amount to carrying on a regulated financial activity. But the response argues that parts of the proposed guidance need greater clarity to ensure that developers, miners, node operators and providers of non-custodial wallets are not inadvertently caught by rules intended for financial intermediaries.

The paper considers where responsibility should lie in decentralised systems, arguing that regulation should follow actual control rather than simply influence over software development. It also examines the position of Bitcoin and Lightning nodes, mining, non-custodial wallets and automated payment routing.

The response also looks at the treatment of Bitcoin payments, including payment processors and merchants accepting Bitcoin, and questions why Bitcoin payment services may face different regulatory treatment from those involving qualifying stablecoins.

The central argument is that Bitcoin businesses should be regulated for the financial services they provide, not simply for participating in or maintaining the Bitcoin network.

📄 Read the full written paper here:

👉  Response to the FCA's Consultation Paper Response to the FCA's Consultation Paper

To find out more about Bitcoin Policy UK's work and how you can get involved, visit:

https://bitcoinpolicy.uk/

item.title: Quantum Bitcoin Countdown – Bitcoin Has Until 2032 | Isabel Foxen Duke QBC Ep. 13
item.description: BIP-360 proposes the first step toward a quantum-resistant Bitcoin: a new output type built to carry quantum-resistant signatures in a later upgrade. Which signature scheme follows, and how quickly developers can agree on it, is still under debate. So is Bitcoin ready for quantum, and how much time does it have? In the 13th episode of The Quantum Bitcoin Podcast, Bitcoin historian Pete Rizzo and co-host Nathan Jeffay put that question to Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, adviser to the Starknet Foundation and co-author of BIP-360, who says Bitcoin should be prepared by 2032 and that the push to get there has accelerated sharply in the past year.Episode 13 is the one that follows the fix through Bitcoin’s proposal process: how BIP-360 shrank from a single moonshot proposal into a step-by-step upgrade path, why some developers now question whether anything else deserves their time, and why she argues that for Bitcoin the conservative choice is to change the protocol. She explains the stateful and stateless halves of SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a quantum-resistant signature, why the safer stateless path could cost 10 to 20 times today’s fees, and why custodians and most wallets are expected to avoid the stateful path. It covers how miners are approaching the threat, why the first quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction calmed the market without settling the problem, what could happen to the millions of coins that never move, and the wallet habits that protect holders today. It closes with her response to Chamath Palihapitiya’s criticism of Bitcoin’s progress, her 2032 timeline, and why she expects shocks to the market even in the best-prepared case.The Quantum Bitcoin Podcast is a series examining the quantum threat to Bitcoin, designed to be watched in sequence. Each episode opens with a discussion between the hosts, presents extended interviews with expert guests on a single key question, and closes with a recap of how the evidence has changed their thinking.Links referenced:MARA Foundation - [link]BIP-360 - [link]SHRINCS / OP_CHECKSHRINCS - [link]Quantum Safe Bitcoin (QSB) paper - [link]Google Quantum AI, “Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies against Quantum Vulnerabilities” - [link]Chamath Palihapitiya on Bitcoin and quantum - [link]Justin Drake on address reuse - [link]https://www.nist.gov/pqcryptoEpisodes referencedJonas Nick - [link]Charles Guillemet - [link]Avihu Levy - [link]Eli Ben-Sasson - [link]Nic Carter - [link]Cryptography and physicshttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shor%27s_algorithmhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover%27s_algorithmhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliptic_Curve_Digital_Signature_Algorithmhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-quantum_cryptographyhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash-based_cryptographyhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lattice-based_cryptographyhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fork_(blockchain)https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computingCHAPTERS0:00 Intro5:32 How BIP 360 Evolved9:32 Choosing Post-Quantum Signature Schemes13:23 Stateful Versus Stateless Wallet Trade-Offs26:34 Are Bitcoin Miners Preparing28:12 Quantum-Safe Bitcoin Transactions Today31:58 Why Unmoved Coins Matter34:39 Wallet Hygiene and Address Reuse38:16 Consensus and the 2032 Timeline43:28 Where to Follow the ResearchGUESTSIsabel Foxen Duke is the head of the MARA Foundation and an adviser to the Starknet Foundation. She co-authored BIP-360, the proposal for a quantum-resistant Bitcoin output type, alongside Hunter Beast and Ethan Heilman, and began working on quantum resistance at MARA through a quantum-resistant sidechain project.FOLLOWThe Quantum Bitcoin Podcast: https://www.youtube.com/@QuantumBitcoinPodcastPete Rizzo: https://x.com/pete_rizzo_Isabel Foxen Duke: https://x.com/IsabelFoxenDukeMARA Foundation: [link]Anduro: [link]New episodes release weekly. item.title: CryptoFlip | Bitcoin, Crypto & Trading – How Binance Lost $6,300,000,000 in 3 minutes
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Binance just took a six billion dollar hit. If they can go after the biggest exchange in crypto, they can go after anyone.

If your crypto sits on an exchange, this episode is about you.

Binance says user funds are safe and it has the money to cover the hit. Good. If it happens to your account, nobody's covering you.

Ricardo breaks down how the attackers got in and how fast the money moved. Deji makes the bear case for Bitcoin. Then each of us say what we'd do with money sitting on Binance.


Ricardo closes with his hot take. AI is going to steal all our crypto.


Not financial advice. No buy or sell calls, just how I protect my own money.

item.title: Christian Faith & Bitcoin -Exploring Bible Money, Christian Money And Faith In Jesus Connect – Who Keeps the Record? Bitcoin, Trust and a God Who Doesn’t Change
item.description:
Your money isn’t really in your bank. It’s an entry in someone else’s ledger. In this episode, Myles uses the stone money of Yap to show what money is beneath the coins and cards, explains in plain English how Bitcoin keeps an honest record without asking you to trust anyone, and considers what a God who never lies and never shows favouritism has to say about it all. No technical background required.

Get intouch: ⁠faithandbitcoin@gmail.com⁠

Check the website: ⁠faithandbitcoin.com

Scriptures in this episode:

  • Numbers 23:19: God does not lie or change his mind
  • Leviticus 19:15: no partiality to the poor or favouritism to the powerful
  • Proverbs 13:11: wealth gathered little by little will grow
  • Proverbs 27:23: know well the condition of your flocks
  • 1 Thessalonians 5:21: test everything and hold fast to what is good

item.title: The Bitcoin IFA Podcast – #28 Peter Lane | Bitcoin Life | How Offshore Bonds Solve the Bitcoin Inheritance Tax Problem for IFAs
item.description:
What do you do with your Bitcoin when you die?
 
Peter Lane has spent years building the answer. He launched Europe's first spot Bitcoin ETF on Euronext Amsterdam in 2023. Now, as founder of Bitcoin Life, granted a full life insurance licence by the Guernsey Financial Services Commission in September 2026, he's created the first regulated offshore bond designed specifically for Bitcoin.
 
This episode is essential listening for any financial adviser with clients who hold Bitcoin.
 
Peter and Dan cover:
 
 - The four-year cycle: why Peter believes the sellers are already exhausted, and what that means for Q4 2026
 - Why Bitcoin is now a 'forever asset', and what that means for estate planning
 - The offshore bond explained: how this 200-year-old structure now has a Bitcoin version
 - Using a loan trust to move Bitcoin outside your estate, and why paying CGT now could save a fortune in IHT later
 - The probate problem: executors have a strict legal duty to find all estate assets, including Bitcoin. What happens when they can't?
 - Custody: how BitGo holds the Bitcoin within the structure, and why self-custody doesn't work inside a trust
 - The expat opportunity: UK nationals living abroad with zero CGT who can structure Bitcoin outside their estate before returning home
 - Why financial advisers were never taught what money is, and what that means for their ability to advise clients on Bitcoin
 - The commercial risk of not engaging with Bitcoin: Peter's tomato analogy explains exactly why 'I don't like it' is not a professional position

To speak with Pete about putting your client's Bitcoin into an offshore bond for you or your clients, click here - https://bitcoinlife.co.uk/?utm_source=bitcoin_ifa&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=launch&utm_content=newsletter

Speak with The Bitcoin Adviser about Custody Solutions - https://content.thebitcoinadviser.com/the-bitcoin-ifa


Sign up to my newsletter - https://hub.thebitcoinifa.com/newsletter


Website - www.thebitcoinifa.com


We always recommend watching ‘What’s the Problem’ by Joe Bryan:

https://bit.ly/jbwtp

This podcast is for FCA-authorised financial advisers only and is not for retail clients.

item.title: Bitcoin Well Podcast – BlackRock’s New Bitcoin ETF Is a Derivative of a Derivative | Adam O'Brien
item.description:
Bitcoin is holding above $80,000 heading into this conversation, 916 days past the halving, and the spot ETFs just bled more than $600 million in a single day without the price barely flinching. Q is joined by Bitcoin Well CEO Adam O'Brien, back from Bitcoin for Financial Services in Denver, to explain why the bigger story is what Wall Street is building on top of bitcoin.

Q argues that BlackRock's newly filed PBIT, a buffer ETF that trades options against IBIT to absorb roughly the first 10% of losses while capping your upside, is the mortgage-backed security of bitcoin: a derivative of a derivative, and the kind of product that could drive the next big crash. Adam walks through why Larry Fink came out of 2008 more powerful than he went in, what JPMorgan's first-ever bitcoin forecast (10% a year in the bear case, roughly 17% in the bull case) really tells you about bank incentives, and why a lowball forecast might one day carry legal risk. We get into Jamie Dimon's pivot from threatening to fire bitcoin buyers to pricing bitcoin into his long-term outlook, why ETF outflows aren't moving the price the way the headlines claim, and why every asset except bitcoin sits on the first rung of the counterparty ladder, including the option to hold real bitcoin in your IRA instead of the ETF.

This is a sharp conversation about Wall Street, ETFs, and counterparty risk, for anyone trying to understand who actually stands between them and their money.

item.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute – Travis Fisher, Marty Bent and Thomas Pacchia: Powering It All
item.description:
Can the power grid keep up with AI without leaving ratepayers with the bill? Marty Bent and Travis Fisher join Thomas Pacchia to discuss grid capacity, private power, permitting and what AI infrastructure can learn from Bitcoin mining.

CHAPTERS
00:00 Introduction
00:45 Lessons from Bitcoin mining
02:24 The strongest critiques of rapid grid growth
04:24 Private grids and off-grid experimentation
06:46 Who pays if demand falls short?
07:21 Moving compute toward available power
09:17 Flexibility, storage, and permitting reform
12:20 Political risk and AI’s economic role

Session: Powering It All
Recorded during Day 2 of Freedom Tech DC 2026, September 23, 2026, in Washington, DC.
Presented by the Bitcoin Policy Institute.

SPEAKERS
Thomas Pacchia — Co-Founder, PubKey; moderator
Travis Fisher — Director of Energy and Environmental Policy Studies, Cato Institute
Marty Bent — Managing Partner, Ten31

item.title: Bitcoin Audible.DE - Die besten Bitcoin-Artikel, vorgelesen in deutscher Sprache! – 209. Cory Klippsten - Die Welt, die Bitcoin aufbauen wird
item.description:
von Cory Klippsten – Originaltitel: «The World Bitcoin Will Build«

«Niemand wird unsere ‚Bright Orange Future‘ für uns machen.
Wir müssen es selbst tun.»

(Cory Klippsten)

«Fix the money, fix the world.» Repariere das Geldsystem –
repariere die Welt. Das weltweit erste und größte dezentrale Geldnetzwerk könnte eine lebendigere und gerechtere Gesellschaft einleiten. item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 24) ... Energie mit zwei Leben
item.description:
Bitcoin und Energieverbrauch werden oft in einem negativen Zusammenhang genannt. Diese Folge zeigt ein differenzierteres Bild: warum Bitcoin-Mining Stromnetze stabilisieren kann, wie aus Abwärme ein zweiter Wertschöpfungskreislauf entsteht, und wo die Grenzen dieser Entwicklung aktuell noch liegen.

Themen in dieser Folge:

  • Wie sich der Anteil nachhaltiger Energien beim Bitcoin-Mining seit 2022 entwickelt hat
  • Warum der Ausbau von Wind- und Solarenergie ein Netzstabilitätsproblem mit sich bringt
  • Wie Bitcoin-Miner als flexible Last genutzt werden können, um Lastspitzen abzupuffern
  • Warum jede Kilowattstunde beim Mining "zwei Leben" bekommt: Bitcoin-Belohnung und nutzbare Wärme
  • Drei Unternehmen, die das bereits umsetzen: Terahash, 21energy und Power2Bit


Die Anfangs erwähnte Studie der Cambridge University

https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/2025/cambridge-study-sustainable-energy-rising-in-bitcoin-mining/


Erwähnte Unternehmen:

  • Terahash – Bitcoin-Mining Infrastruktur für Unternehmen
  • 21energy – Bitcoin-Heizungen für Privathaushalte und Kleingewerbe
  • Power2Bit – flexible, klimaneutrale Rechenzentren und kommunale Wärmeplanung


Hinweis: Die genannten Prozentzahlen zum Energiemix variieren je nach Berechnungsmethode (konservativer Netzmix vs. direkte Unternehmensmeldungen) und waren zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme aktuell.

item.title: The Mustard Seed Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin Could Reach $840,000 Within Five Years | Sam Baker
item.description:
Sam Baker, research analyst at River, joins me to explain why Bitcoin could reach $840,000 within the next three to five years. We discuss the institutional adoption and capital inflows behind River’s model, the case for a 10% Bitcoin allocation, why each dollar invested can add several dollars to Bitcoin’s market cap, custody considerations, the CLARITY Act, AI’s role in accelerating macro trends, and why businesses are currently driving Bitcoin demand.

item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

item.title: Bitcoin Monfalcone Podcast – 22.Bitcoin, libertà monetaria ed economia del buon senso: perché il sistema Fiat ci rende più poveri
item.description:
Esiste davvero libertà politica senza libertà economica? E può esistere libertà economica senza libertà monetaria?

In questa puntata affrontiamo uno dei temi più profondi e meno discussi: il rapporto tra moneta, proprietà, libertà e responsabilità individuale. Partendo dai principi della scuola economica austriaca, analizziamo perché il sistema monetario attuale basato su euro, dollari e banche centrali tende a distruggere il risparmio, aumentare il debito e ridurre il potere d’acquisto delle persone.

Parliamo di economia del buon senso, del ruolo della moneta nella società e del motivo per cui inflazione e stampa monetaria non sono fenomeni neutri ma strumenti che trasferiscono ricchezza da chi produce e risparmia a chi riceve il denaro per primo.

In questa puntata scoprirai:

  • Perché la moneta è la pietra angolare della libertà
  • Cosa insegna davvero la scuola economica austriaca
  • Perché oro e argento sono stati moneta per migliaia di anni
  • Come nasce il denaro e perché non dovrebbe essere monopolio dello Stato
  • Perché il denaro Fiat perde continuamente valore
  • Cosa significa davvero inflazione
  • Perché Bitcoin rappresenta una forma di moneta sana, scarsa e non manipolabile
  • Il legame tra proprietà privata, libertà economica e responsabilità personale
  • Perché Bitcoin ti permette di essere davvero la banca di te stesso
  • La differenza tra possedere davvero qualcosa e dipendere da intermediari

Bitcoin non è solo tecnologia. È una nuova idea di proprietà, libertà e responsabilità individuale. È la prima forma di denaro digitale che non dipende da governi, banche o autorizzazioni centrali e che può essere custodita direttamente da chi la possiede.

Bitcoin Monfalcone nasce proprio per aiutare privati, famiglie, aziende ed esercenti a capire questi concetti in modo semplice, concreto e senza tecnicismi. Organizziamo incontri gratuiti, serate pratiche e momenti di confronto per spiegare come funziona davvero il denaro e perché Bitcoin può rappresentare un’alternativa concreta.

Per approfondire:

  • Sito: www.bitcoinmonfalcone.it
  • Telegram: https://t.me/BitcoinMonfalcone

item.title: Der Bitcoin Kompass: Wegweiser im Kaninchenbau – Folge 5: Der Bitcoin-Preis – Zwischen Angebot, Nachfrage und Geldpolitik
item.description:
Was bestimmt eigentlich den Bitcoin-Preis? In Folge 5 vom Bitcoin-Kompass sprechen wir üeber eines der meistdiskutierten Themen im Bitcoin-Space: den Preis. Dabei geht es nicht um Prognosen oder Kaufempfehlungen, sondern um ein grundlegendes Verständnis dafüer, wie der Bitcoin-Preis entsteht und welche Kraefte ihn beeinflussen.


Wir erklären, wie Angebot und Nachfrage auf Bitcoin-Börsen funktionieren, warum das Handelsvolumen oft wichtiger ist als der Preis selbst und welche Rolle die Marktkapitalisierung spielt. Ausserdem beleuchten wir die grossen Einflussfaktoren: das Bitcoin-Halving und den Vier-Jahres-Zyklus, die Geldpolitik der US-Notenbank (Fed), Inflation und die wachsenden Staatsschulden der USA. Im Vergleich zwischen Bitcoin und Gold zeigen sie, warum Bitcoin technologisch ueberlegen sein könnte - und warum der Preis letztlich ein Spiegel des wachsenden Vertrauens in diese neue Technologie ist.


Mehr Infos, interaktive Grafiken zur Marktkapitalisierung und Kontaktmoeglichkeiten findet ihr auf:


Webseite: https://derbitcoinkompass.ch

E-Mail: kontakt@derbitcoinkompass.ch

Telegram: https://t.me/btc_kaninchenbau


Feedback und Fragen gerne per E-Mail, ueber Telegram oder ueber unsere Webseite.



(00:00:00) Begruessung & Einfuehrung ins Thema Preis

(00:01:31) Volatilitaet und der aktuelle Bitcoin-Preis

(00:02:33) Kaufkraft, Inflation und warum Menschen investieren

(00:05:20) Marktkapitalisierung: Bitcoin vs. Gold vs. Immobilien vs. Aktien

(00:08:05) Wie entsteht der Bitcoin-Preis? Angebot & Nachfrage erklaert

(00:11:04) Warum das Handelsvolumen entscheidend ist

(00:12:43) Die grossen Einflussfaktoren auf den Bitcoin-Preis

(00:13:26) In was messen wir den Preis? Euro, Dollar oder Aepfel?

(00:17:03) Warum Geld kein stabiler Massstab ist

(00:18:10) Bitcoins festes Angebot: Maximal 21 Millionen

(00:20:02) Das Halving und der Vier-Jahres-Zyklus

(00:24:22) Die Fed, Zinspolitik und US-Staatsschulden

(00:31:27) Was bedeutet das alles fuer den Bitcoin-Preis?

(00:33:37) Bitcoin vs. Gold: Vorteile und Unterschiede

(00:40:30) Preisprognose: Bitcoin auf 1 Million Dollar?

(00:41:54) Zusammenfassung & Verabschiedung

item.title: Store of Bitcoin - Bitcoin as Store of Value – Ep. 49 - Daniel Batten | A new different wave of Bitcoin Adopters.
item.description:
In this episode of Store of Bitcoin, host Alessandro Ottaviani welcomes Daniel Batten, a prominent Bitcoin analyst and investor, to discuss the evolving narrative surrounding Bitcoin, particularly in relation to energy consumption and environmental impact. Daniel shares insights on how the mainstream media's perception of Bitcoin has shifted from skepticism to a more favorable view, largely due to rigorous research and advocacy from the Bitcoin community. He emphasizes the importance of effectively communicating Bitcoin's benefits to various stakeholders, including policymakers and investors, to foster broader adoption.

The conversation delves into the challenges of reaching new adopters, particularly those who may not be motivated by the same values that initially attracted early Bitcoin enthusiasts. Daniel highlights the need for a more nuanced approach to education and outreach, focusing on the social and environmental benefits of Bitcoin. He also discusses the potential for Bitcoin to serve as a tool for financial inclusion in developing countries, where it can provide a safeguard against inflation and empower individuals in oppressive regimes. The episode concludes with a look at future trends in Bitcoin adoption and the importance of aligning messaging with the values of diverse audiences.

This episode is sponsored by ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠BitVault⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠, the new open-source & self-custody wallet utilizing time-delays and multisignature to offset physical attacks and hacks.

item.title: BITCOIN WITTAYA – EP#10_หากจะเกษียณในปี 2030 ต้องเตรียมบิทคอยน์ไว้เท่าไร
item.description:
บทวิเคราะห์และข้อแนะนำเพิ่มเติม

  • ที่มาของตัวเลข: การคาดการณ์มาจากผู้เชี่ยวชาญหลายสำนัก เช่น Bloomberg (กรณีสมจริง), Kathy Wood จาก Ark Invest (ภาษี ETF และวิกฤตธนาคารหนุน) และ Michael Saylor (กรณี Moonshot ที่มอง Bitcoin เป็นสินทรัพย์หลักของโลก)

  • ความเสี่ยงที่ต้องระวัง: แม้ตัวเลขจะดูน่าตื่นเต้น แต่การลงทุนมีความเสี่ยงสูง ไม่ควร "ใส่ไข่ทั้งหมดไว้ในตะกร้าใบเดียว" (All-in) ควรมีการกระจายความเสี่ยงในสินทรัพย์อื่นด้วย

  • ความปลอดภัยสำคัญที่สุด: หากลงทุนใน Bitcoin ควรเก็บรักษาใน Hardware Wallet (Cold Storage) เพื่อป้องกันการถูกแฮ็กหรือปัญหาจากกระดานเทรดล้มละลาย

item.title: Bitcoin Byltingin – #49 - Endurkoman
item.description:
Eftir tæpt ár af pásu sátust við niður og fjölluðu um fréttir úr Bitcoin-heimum síðastliðna mánuði sem og um gang mála þessa dagana. Eitt stærsta málið þessa dagana snýst um nýjustu útgáfu af Bitcoin core client-inu, Core 30 og þá umdeildu ákvörðun teymisis um að hækka svokallað OP_RETURN úr 83 í 100.000 bytes. Mun þessi ákvörðun reynast afdrifarík fyrir framtíð Bitcoin eða er þetta stormur í vatnsglasi? Einnig ræddum við um íslensk fyrirtæki sem taka á móti bitcoin í viðskiptum. Spennandi tímar sem við lifum!

item.title: Beyond Bitcoin – What is Bitcoin
item.description:
Bitcoin can seem mysterious — full of buzzwords like mining, blockchain, and scarcity. But at its core, the ideas are simple.

In this first episode of Beyond Bitcoin, we’ll walk through Bitcoin from the ground up:

• Who created it and why.

• How it shifted from digital cash to digital gold.

• How the blockchain, nodes, and miners keep it running.

• Why scarcity — with only 21 million Bitcoin ever — shapes its unique four-year cycle.

By the end, you’ll have a clear, beginner-friendly understanding of what Bitcoin is, how it works, and why it matters today.

Whether you’re brand new or just curious, this is your entry point into the world of Bitcoin and Beyond.

In this first episode of Beyond Bitcoin, we’ll walk through Bitcoin from the ground up:

• Who created it and why.

• How it shifted from digital cash to digital gold.

• How the blockchain, nodes, and miners keep it running.

• Why scarcity — with only 21 million Bitcoin ever — shapes its unique four-year cycle.

By the end, you’ll have a clear, beginner-friendly understanding of what Bitcoin is, how it works, and why it matters today.

Whether you’re brand new or just curious, this is your entry point into the world of Bitcoin and Beyond.

item.title: Two Hearts One Bitcoin – What is the Lightning Network
item.description:
Ever wonder how Bitcoin could actually work for everyday payments? Enter the Lightning Network — Bitcoin’s current solution for scaling. In this episode, we break down what the Lightning Network is, how it works, and why it’s kind of like running a bar tab instead of paying after every single drink. (Trust us, it’ll make sense.) We get a little technical, but whether you’re curious or confused, this one’s for you.


📢 Disclaimer: This podcast is for educational and entertainment purposes only. We’re not financial advisors, and nothing in this episode should be considered financial or investment advice. Always do your own research before making any financial decisions.

item.title: Bitcoin Bottom Line – The Increasing Need for Decentralized Systems with C.J. Wilson & Josh Olszewicz
item.description:
In this week’s episode of Bitcoin Bottom Line, hosts C.J. Wilson and Josh Olszewicz delve into the recent bank closures and their impact on the crypto space. The issues raised from these closures are not unique, and people are looking for someone to blame. Olszewicz states, “I believe the FED plays a big role in this because they had to catch up after slowly raising the rate. Ultimately it's the bank's problem. It is their job to manage that risk appropriately.” People have been dependent that the FED will continue on a steady track of raising rate, but this has not been the case. 

Throughout the highs and lows of Bitcoin, people have continued to show their faith and commitment to the fight for economic freedom. Public opinion of Bitcoin is at a low, with recent scandals causing hate and distrust towards crypto. Wilson describes those who have persevered through the valleys as “those who have proven their worth with strong hands is a bear market.” Now it is time for Bitcoiners to have discipline and avoid shorting during the highs. As Bitcoiners immerse themselves in the space, they grow more skeptical of traditional banks, questioning the rate of fees and if the deal is truly beneficial long term. Wilson states, “Everything is good for Bitcoin as long as it continues to function uninterrupted.” 

Wilson and Olszewicz go on to discuss credit unions, the importance of financial education from a young age, and regulations. Many large corporations have begun moving offshore to countries with fewer regulations, but Wilson warns that they must plan for long-term alterations. Historically, large corporations have used this strategy successfully for years, but crypto companies have to be selective with the location to ensure they will not be suddenly changing their regulations. The likelihood of the country benefiting from growth-based crypto companies should be taken into consideration.

Listen to the full episode for more!

item.title: Clubhouse Bitcoin Nederland – Special Guest - Paul Buitink
item.description: Paul Buitink is een bekend gezicht in de wereld van goud en financiële alternatieven. Hij levert met regelmaat zijn bijdragen in de media zoals BNR Cryptocast en op zijn eigen Twitter- en YouTube-kanaal ‘Reinvent Money’. Ook was hij een van de initiatiefnemers van de depositobank, een full reservebank. Paul heeft (internationale) ervaring in edelmetaal opgedaan bij Goldmoney en werkte als Senior Commercial Manager bij Atradius. Sinds 1 augustus is Managing Director van Aunexum Precious Metal Group.

item.title: Breaking Through Barriers Hosted by Bitcoin Gal, Amanda Mirus – Episode 6: Music, Passion, & Activism. So Help Me (God) by Jedidiah aka JedStarrr Hosted by Amanda Mirus
item.description:
This week on Breaking Through Barriers, I had the pleasure of interviewing Jedidiah aka JedStarrr. The music genius behind the new album, So Help Me (God).

Jedidiah (a.k.a. JedStarrr) is a music producer from Brooklyn, New York. Who has been producing music for the last decade. With his unique style of experimental beats and film score influence sounds, his skill set wasn't built overnight. 

He's received attention from the likes of Metroboomin, Mase, Keyshia Cole, & Big Sean. His influences stems from the likes of legendary artists like Kanye West, Timbaland, Rapsody, & The Roots.
When listening to his music, you can hear the effort to create a "timeless record" rather than "today's hit".

The goal for JedStarrr now, as he transitions to taking on a heavier songwriter load is to energize his fan base to stay empowered through their art. His subject matter typically wraps around dense topics like today's political & social economy in America, Religion, Faith, and guidance. 

He started off as a drummer at the age of 14 and now in his mid 20s hes on course to being one of Hip Hop's most intriguing producer/artist!

Hear some of his journey on this weeks episode and listen/download his music on all streaming platforms. JedStarrr, So Help Me (God)

Instagram @JedStarrr

All Music, Including his new album So Help Me (God)
